## Goal

Prevent the audit runner's Phase-1 code-quality scan from passing non-Python files (YAML, JSON, Markdown, etc.) to ruff as explicit file arguments, eliminating false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings that get auto-created as work items.

## Background / Root cause

On 2026-08-11, an implement self-review audit ran `run_code_quality(files=cq_scope_files)` with the git changed-file list, which included `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` (uncommitted changes at the time). `_run_ruff_check` invoked `ruff check <yaml-file>` — ruff parses YAML as Python and emitted 121 false-positive `invalid-syntax` findings, which `create_epics_for_findings` auto-created as work items under the Quality Improvement epic (LP-0MSJFTRUW0076Z5Y). Those stale items were later marked completed/in_review and drained one-by-one by the herdr downtime audit tier (~59 dispatches in one evening).

The `.ruff.toml` `exclude = ["*.yaml", "*.yml"]` fix (commit 7580063) is **insufficient**: ruff only honors `exclude` for directory scans; explicit file arguments bypass it (verified: `ruff check config-cheap.yaml` with the exclude in place still returns invalid-syntax findings, while `ruff check .` returns `[]`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `run_ruff` / `_run_ruff_check` filter the `files` list to Python extensions (`.py`, `.pyi`, `.ipynb`) before invoking ruff; non-Python files are skipped and never passed as explicit paths.
2. A regression test asserts ruff is never invoked with a `.yaml`/`.yml` file path when the changed-file list includes one, and that no finding work items are created for non-Python files.
3. Directory-scan behavior (`files=None`) is unchanged.
4. Genuine ruff findings on `.py` files are unaffected (existing tests pass).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MT2Q10PX0078DEM** – Ruff: exclude YAML & non-Python files additively across all projects (whole-project scan) (completed)
- **SA-0MQPP6TFJ008LU1N** – wl close: add recovery path for done parent with open children (completed)
- **SA-0MRIIQLQI001RQVB** – Refactor command/doc.md for conciseness (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptance, asserts, audit, auto, background (+90 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, audit, auto, behavior, bypass (+89 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: acceptance, audit, auto, background, behavior (+80 more)

data.description:
## Problem

`resolve_pytest_command()` in `skill/test_runner.py` prefers a PATH-resolved bare
`pytest` over the interpreter that starts the runner. On a host where
`~/.local/bin/pytest` carries a system-Python shebang (`#!/usr/bin/python3`;
PEP 668 externally managed, no project dependencies), the test skill and the
audit F3 auto-run execute the suite under an interpreter that cannot import the
project's dependencies. Collection then fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` and
exit 2 even though the same tree is green under the repository's canonical
runner, which calls `python3 -m pytest`.

Observed on host `RossGameDev` against ContentCreator: 13 collection errors
(`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy'` from
`.pi/skills/wiki-tts-generate/scripts/tts_generate.py`, plus
`tests/test_podcast_parts_layout.py`, `tests/test_rss_process_notes.py`) versus
2588 passed / 16 skipped via `./scripts/run_tests.sh`. The red result is cached
by git state and scope, so one such run poisons the audit-accepted full-suite
entry for that commit until a `--force` run replaces it.

## Users

- **Agent running `/skill:test`** — needs the suite result to describe the
  project's real test state, not PATH ordering.
- **Agent running the audit F3 gate** — needs a green cached full-suite entry
  instead of `missing` and a manual fallback.
- **Producer / maintainer** — needs one documented interpreter rule shared by
  every project, instead of per-repository workarounds.

User story: *As an agent running the test skill on a host whose PATH order
differs from the project's documented runner, I want pytest executed by the
interpreter that carries the project's dependencies, so that a green result
means green and the cache records a trustworthy entry.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — Resolution order is: `PYTEST_BIN`, then `TEST_PYTHON`, then
  `sys.executable -m pytest`, then bare `pytest` on PATH, then
  `python3 -m pytest`. Each candidate is used only when the earlier forms
  cannot run pytest (probed, not assumed).
- **AC2** — When bare `pytest` resolves to an interpreter that cannot run
  pytest (or cannot import the project's dependencies), it is not selected
  while an earlier candidate works, and the interpreter actually used is
  recorded in the run output and in the cache entry so the choice is auditable.
- **AC3** — Regression tests in `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py` cover:
  (a) `sys.executable -m pytest` winning over a PATH `pytest` bound to a
  different interpreter; (b) `PYTEST_BIN` and `TEST_PYTHON` override winning
  over every other form; (c) the existing `which`-first and `~/.local/bin`
  fallback tests updated to the new precedence; (d) the memoised cache still
  returning the resolved command.
- **AC4** — On host `RossGameDev`,
  `python3 <skill>/test/scripts/run_tests.py --type full --force` reports the
  same green result as `./scripts/run_tests.sh` in ContentCreator, and names
  the interpreter used.
- **AC5** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`).
- **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Additive, never weakening.** Resolution must never select a candidate that
  cannot run pytest; no suite may be silently narrowed or skipped.
- **Canonical command form is unchanged.** `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings`
  stays the stable form used for cache keying and cross-consumer reuse; only
  the executable prefix varies, per the existing `executable_test_command()`
  contract.
- **Preserve the reason the bare-`pytest` rule exists.** SA-0MSQ012QG005N22S
  added it because user-site bin dirs (`~/.local/bin`) are absent from
  non-login shells. `sys.executable -m pytest` and the retained
  `~/.local/bin` fallback both keep that case working.
- **Out of scope:** ContentCreator-specific suite pinning (`.pi/test-config.json`
  → `suiteCommands`) is tracked in `OSL-0MVJOKJXK009J8ZA`. This item changes
  the shared skill only.

## Existing state

- `resolve_pytest_command()` order today: `shutil.which("pytest")` →
  `~/.local/bin/pytest` (when executable) → `python3 -m pytest`, memoised in
  `_PYTEST_COMMAND`.
- `executable_test_command()` rewrites only the executable prefix at run time.
- `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py` asserts the current precedence,
  including `test_resolve_pytest_command_uses_which_when_on_path`.
- No `PYTEST_BIN` or `TEST_PYTHON` support exists anywhere in the tree.

## Desired change

Implement the resolution order in AC1 with real candidate probing, an explicit
per-invocation override, the selected interpreter surfaced in run output and
cache metadata, and updated tests plus documentation. Update
`test_resolve_pytest_command_uses_which_when_on_path` to the new precedence
rather than deleting it.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test_runner.py` — `resolve_pytest_command()`, `executable_test_command()`, probe/caching helpers
- `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py` — new and updated regression tests
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `PYTEST_CMD`, cache entry metadata (record chosen interpreter)
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — document resolution order, overrides, and cache metadata

## Risks and assumptions

- **Blast radius.** Every project that uses the skill inherits this change.
  Mitigation: unit tests cover each precedence step and the cache.
- **Probe cost.** Probing candidates spawns a subprocess. Mitigation: keep the
  existing memoisation so probing happens once per process, and probe with
  `-m pytest --version` only.
- **Cache semantics.** The cache key stays git-state + scope (interpreter stays
  informational), so a green entry produced under a different interpreter is
  still visible in its metadata.
- **Assumption.** `sys.executable` is the right default because the skill is
  started with the interpreter the agent selected (`python3 …/run_tests.py`),
  which matches the repository canonical runner.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Repository-specific pinning and dependency installation
  are recorded as separate work items, not folded into this change.

## Related work

- `OSL-0MVJE3HDF003DZ9B` — origin item; closed on creation of this item
  (discovered while verifying AC7 of `OSL-0MT47CNJE008EJGR`).
- `OSL-0MVJOKJXK009J8ZA` — ContentCreator repo-local mitigation
  (`.pi/test-config.json` → `suiteCommands`); complementary, not duplicate.
- `SA-0MSQ012QG005N22S` — original reason a bare `pytest` fallback exists.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (Map → operator, interactive):** "Where should the fix land — framework
  fix in SorraAgents, ContentCreator-only `suiteCommands` pin, or editing the
  SorraAgents checkout from the OSL work item?"
  **Answer (operator):** "A, no need to keep this item open, close as soon as
  the SorraAgents item is created." Source: interactive reply.
  Outcome: framework fix here; `OSL-0MVJE3HDF003DZ9B` closed on creation.
- **Q2 (Map → operator, interactive):** "Interpreter selection policy in
  `resolve_pytest_command()` — override → `sys.executable -m pytest` → PATH
  `pytest` → `python3 -m pytest`, or alternatives?"
  **Answer (operator):** "A". Source: interactive reply.
  Outcome: precedence recorded in AC1.

## Goal

As a producer, I want `wl sync` to complete in the SorraAgents checkout so locally-authored work items publish, and I want `refs/worklog/data` to stay free of sentinel-authored commits so fresh clones can sync at all.

## Issue

`wl sync` refused to merge inbound worklog data:

```
✗ Sync failed: Refusing to merge worklog data from refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data: 2 incoming commit(s) fail the author-identity gate.
- 893203e8d: author email 't@t.com' does not match configured user.email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com'
- dec50d4d6: author email 't@t.com' does not match configured user.email '250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com'
```

The gate is correct (sentinel `t@t.com` must stay refused); the *data on the ref* was the problem.

## Resolution (operator-authorised 2026-10-23: "Yes clear the sync block")

Option (b) from the SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2 playbook — re-author the sentinel commits on `refs/worklog/data`, trees untouched, force-push with lease. No `--allow-foreign-author` was used.

1. Backed up the pre-rewrite tip as tag `worklog-tt-reauthor-backup-2026-10-23`.
2. `git filter-branch --env-filter` rewrote every `t@t.com` author/committer to `Sorra the Orc <250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com>` on a temp ref.
   Verified before pushing: `git diff --quiet <old> <new>` → identical trees, commits 2317 → 2317, sentinel authors 2 → 0.
3. Force-pushed with `--force-with-lease` (4 attempts — concurrent agent syncs kept advancing the ref; every attempt re-fetched, re-rewrote and re-verified the tree before pushing).
4. Two recovery deltas published on the rewritten ref to restore records the pre-rewrite remote held but the local store lacked:
   - delta 1: 2 items + 6 comments (`SA-0MT7U2SN9007Z112`, `SA-0MT7U3NCB000T1SR` + their comments, plus comments on `SA-0MT9607Q5009JA2V`, `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL`, `SA-0MVL2NH1G0094FA2`);
   - delta 2: the 3 comments whose parent item was absent from delta 1 (added with byte-identical local parent records) — `wl`'s merge drops comments whose parent item is not in the same delta.
5. Plain `wl sync` (no flags) now succeeds and advances `last-synced-ref`; run repeatedly, no refusals.

## Verification

- Remote history author population: `2305 × 250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `16 × pi@local` (allow-listed), `0 × t@t.com`.
- Tip tree after rewrite is byte-identical to the pre-rewrite tip tree (`git diff --quiet` empty).
- `scripts/check_git_identity.py --repo-root .` → `OK: git identity is consistent`.
- `syncAllowedAuthors` unchanged: the sentinel quarantine is preserved; `t@t.com` is still refused.
- Data fidelity: all 8 previously-missing records verified present via `wl show` (2 items, 6 comments); no items lost in either direction.
- Fresh-clone gate: whole-history author scan is now clean, so a new clone no longer refuses.

## Recurrence

The two offending commits were pushed 2026-10-23 15:41 and 19:18 from an environment still using the incident sentinel identity — consistent with the RossGameDev checkout identified in SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2. Local checkouts and all worktrees on this host report the correct identity, and every concurrent sync on this host during the remediation authored commits correctly. The push-side guard (SA-0MVKMVIAK005981E) is therefore still the durable prevention, and RossGameDev's `user.email` still needs correcting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1** The two sentinel-authored inbound worklog commits are re-authored with the project identity and force-pushed with operator approval; tip tree unchanged.
- [x] **AC2** `wl sync` (no flags) completes — pull and push — and local worklog mutations publish (`last-synced-ref` advances past the rewritten tip).
- [x] **AC3** `t@t.com` remains absent from `syncAllowedAuthors`; `scripts/check_git_identity.py` still treats it as a sentinel.
- [x] **AC4** The recurrence source is explained (non-host checkout still on the sentinel identity; concurrent host syncs are clean) and the prevention item SA-0MVKMVIAK005981E remains open.
- [x] **AC5** No worklog data lost: 2 items and 6 comments restored and verified; remote history author population is clean.

# Tests: drive recovery test harness + terminal regression

## Goal

Establish injectable drive-loop test fixtures covering `finishing_failed` parent reports and green-now regression tests, so the bounded-recovery behaviour (SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY) can be developed test-first. This is the test/verification slice and must land before the implementation features.

## Problem statement

`tests/test_implement_drive.py` already provides the `ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner` fixture pattern for `phase_drive`, but no fixture scripts a `phase_parent` report with `finishing_failed: True` (the livelock entry point), and no test asserts that terminal children are never finished, reset, or re-spawned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- 0. Traceability — covers parent AC5: 5. **Terminal children never touched.** A child already in a terminal stage is never `finished`, reset, or re-spawned (regression guard; the existing `skip-terminal` precedence is preserved and covered by a test).
- 0. Traceability — covers parent AC6: 6. **Tests pass.** New unit tests cover: bounded-finish-attempts, finish-failure→terminal reconciliation, finish-failure→non-terminal reset+continue, terminal-child regression, and truthful reporting (drive-loop fixtures with injectable `parent_runner`/`spawn_session`). Existing `skill/implement/tests/` drive/parent tests continue to pass.
- 1. New test file `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` reuses the `ScriptedParent` / `RecordingSpawner` pattern and the `implement_mod` fixture from `tests/test_implement_drive.py`, exercising `phase_drive` with injectable `parent_runner` / `spawn_session`.
- 2. A fake `parent_runner` fixture can script a report carrying `finishing_failed: True` (with `success: False`, `next_child`, `message`) for a given child — the exact shape emitted by `_run_finish`.
- 3. Regression test (green on current code): a child already terminal (`completed`/`done` status, `in_review` stage, or soft-deleted via `deletedBy`) is never `finish`ed, reset, or re-spawned by drive; the `skip-terminal` precedence in `_classify_child` is preserved and covered by the test.
- 4. Existing `tests/test_implement_drive.py` and `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py` continue to pass.
- 5. Full test suite green for the changed scope (dev-push gate).

## Key Files

- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — new fixtures + regression tests.
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` — existing fixture pattern to reuse (do not modify unless the shared helper must be extracted).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_drive`, `_classify_child` (read-only in this item).

## Constraints

- No behaviour change to `phase_drive` / `phase_parent` in this item (implementation lands in the sibling features). Only fixtures + regression test.
- Reuse existing conventions (`implement_mod` fixture, `mock.patch` of `wl_show` / `wl_show_children` / `_discover_worktree`).

## Related work

- Parent: SA-0MVLIZ33M009C5QY (AC5 regression guard, AC6 test coverage).
- Blocks: the bounded-attempt / reconciliation / reset features below.

## Problem

`skill/ship/scripts/release/regenerate-version.js` runs the consumer repo's `npm run build`, then stages with `git add -u` and commits `Regenerate derived version files for v<version>`. When the consumer repo has a git submodule whose build mutates it (e.g. `npm run build` runs `engine:sync`, which advances `./core` to the engine remote tip — main-street's `build` script does exactly this), `git add -u` also stages the submodule **pointer/gitlink**. The derived-files commit then silently bumps the gitlink while the engine pin (`configs/engine-pin.json`) stays unchanged, and the release pin-contract gate fails on the merged tree (observed in the v0.1.22 release attempt, commit `155eead1`: `core` → `9ee194e0` while the pin stayed `d907af9f`).

## Required change (decided in intake MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57)

- **Generic gitlink exclusion (option A)**: after `git add -u`, unstage every staged submodule pointer (mode `160000` in `git diff --cached` / `git ls-files --stage`), so the derived-files commit can never contain a submodule pointer change. Consumer-repo agnostic; works for any submodule (`core`, future ones) with no per-repo configuration.
- **Regression tests in BOTH copies** (option A): authoritative `tests/node/test-regenerate-version.mjs` and skill-local `skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs` gain a submodule fixture (local-path submodule, `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`, mirroring main-street's engine-sync tests): an advanced/dirty submodule checkout must not end up in the derived-files commit, and normal tracked-file regeneration still commits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `regenerateDerivedFiles` never stages submodule pointers: with a fixture repo containing a submodule whose HEAD differs from the recorded gitlink, the derived-files commit contains only regenerated tracked files — the gitlink is unchanged and no commit is made when the only change is the submodule bump.
- Existing behaviour is preserved: no build script → no-op; successful regeneration commits the derived file(s); failing build is non-fatal.
- Both `tests/node/test-regenerate-version.mjs` and `skill/ship/tests/test_regenerate_version.mjs` pass, and the framework's node test suite is green.
- Docs updated as applicable (`docs/dev/release-process.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` derived-files/merge step) noting submodule pointers are excluded from the derived-files commit.

## Constraints

- No change to main-street's `engine:sync`/`engine:verify` design; the pin/verify split (MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED) stays as is.
- The fix must be generic — no `core`-specific hardcoding (alternative B rejected in intake; allow-list C rejected as needing per-repo config).
- Do not alter the release flow's gate ordering (derived-files step stays post-merge, pre-tag).
- Tracks: MS-0MVN0G6VB000ZF57 (tce-main-street worklog) — this MS item is blocked by this SA item.
data.title: Ship release derived-files step must never stage submodule pointer changes (gitlink exclusion)
